crossref.title: Predicting the mechanical properties of spring networks

papers.summary: Derives the elastic continuum of an arbitrary network of Hookean springs from its geometry and topology alone, with the nonaffine deformation of every triangle obtained from a linear system, and compares the resulting Poisson's ratios and Young's moduli with simulations of stretched strips of ordered triangular lattices, a honeycomb that turns re-entrant, and a foam-like disordered lattice that becomes auxetic.
papers.relevance: Spring networks map directly onto truss models, which Stabileo already solves.

ordered lattices, Supplemental Eq. (9) and Fig. 7
exact lattice moduli, Cauchy-Born, rigidity, production-engine agreement

crossref.title: Optimization of the Initial Post‐Buckling Response of Trusses and Frames by an Asymptotic Approach
crossref.venue: International Journal for Numerical Methods in Engineering

papers.summary: Uses Koiter's asymptotic post-buckling expansion in sizing and topology optimization of trusses and frames. Constraining the first two asymptotic coefficients (initial post-buckling slope and curvature) shapes the post-buckling response and lowers imperfection sensitivity, and the same expansion approximates the nonlinear response so that measures such as end-compliance can be optimized.
papers.relevance: Queue item 4. Runs on the production buckling, corotational and arc-length solvers; validated against closed-form post-buckling coefficients of the Roorda frame and our own arc-length path. No public code (in-house implementation per the paper).

crossref.title: Snapping and switching of elastic arches with patterned preferred curvature

papers.summary: Elastica theory and photomechanical experiments on an arch whose preferred curvature varies along its length and in time. A shallow-arch theory projects the curvature pattern onto Euler buckling modes; overlap with the fundamental mode makes the arch snap, other patterns give a continuous switch to a higher mode. Patterns with the largest energy release and the lowest threshold are found, and the same control applies to passive pre-curved arches loaded at the boundaries.
papers.relevance: Queue item 5. The theory's basis is the Euler buckling modes the production engine already computes; passive arches run on the 2D corotational and arc-length solvers. Zenodo record (data and software, CC-BY-4.0 per the record) not yet inspected file by file.

crossref.title: Layout optimization of large-scale pin-jointed frames

papers.summary: Ground-structure layout optimization of trusses is limited by the number of potential members. The paper presents an iterative member-adding method, built on linear-programming column generation, that starts from a sparsely connected ground structure and adds members as needed until the provably optimal layout is reached, handling problems with very large numbers of potential members.
papers.relevance: Truss layout optimization whose optimal layouts can be analysed and checked on Stabileo's truss solver; useful to engineers for early-stage layouts.

crossref.title: Ultralight, ultrastiff mechanical metamaterials

papers.summary: Octet-truss microlattices made by projection microstereolithography from polymers, metals and ceramics. Because their struts carry load axially instead of bending, the materials are very stiff and strong for their low density.
papers.relevance: Stretch- versus bending-dominated lattices are a direct truss and frame comparison on Stabileo's solvers (stiffness against relative density).
